correctness.rationale: Both projectors agree on the tangent space. On the normal space write the complementary oblique maps on each side as graphs [-C;I], [-D;I] in orthonormal coordinates. Their tensor product has squared norm (1+γ_L²)(1+γ_R²); its orthogonal normal component is the identity, so Pythagoras subtracts one to give the squared defect. A product of top right singular vectors gives equality, including when one defect vanishes. For a combined trial/normal compression K with ||K−I||≤e, the normal-to-trial coefficient A⁻¹B has norm at most e/√(1−e²). Indeed for unit normal y with w=A⁻¹By≠0 and x=w/||w||, write a=xᵀAx, b=xᵀBy. Then b=a||w|| and (a−1)²+b²≤e², with maximal b²/a² at a=1−e². Applying this to the two residual-specific compressed spaces gives the stated sharp universal coefficient, not an exact coefficient for every realized input. The 2×2 Gram examples have spectrum 1±e, yield equality for all permitted distortions and can be embedded in 2×3 sketches. For e_L=3/5, e_R=4/5 the three nonzero leakage entries are −1, 3/4, 4/3, with squared norm 481/144. N=0 gives zero without additional embedding; zero distortions and the tolerance frontier follow by substitution. The supplied script was inspected, not run.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The operator argument works for arbitrary one-sided idempotents fixing the trial spaces, even without sketch Grams. For the realized residual estimate compress each Gram K to its trial-plus-residual space as in the frozen hypotheses. If W is the trial space, then for each unit x∈W, dist(x,KW)≤||x−Kx||≤e. The largest principal angle between W and KW therefore has sine at most e; the one-sided complementary projector has norm at most 1/√(1−e²), since the kernel of the trial projector is (KW)⊥. Applying the complementary tensor norm gives (2). This argument uses the combined spaces and does not follow from Carrel–Grigori's Galerkin pairing bound.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: For any projector E with kernel S, E kills S and has compression equal to I on S⊥, so ||E||²=1+||E−P_{S⊥}||² whenever S⊥ is nonzero. Apply this once to each factor I−L and I−R and once to E=(I−R)⊗(I−L), whose kernel is the tangent space. Norm multiplicativity gives (1+γ_L²)(1+γ_R²)−1 without an additional sketch-specific result. In angle variables this is sec²φ_L sec²φ_R−1, with tanφ_i the graph norm.

value.rationale: Leakage control is a natural question, but this particular norm and sharp tolerance are obtained by multiplying two complementary projector norms, subtracting the unit normal component and applying the elementary sharp bound on the angle between a subspace and its near-identity image. Independent two-dimensional equality on each side already realizes the product. No distinct scientific remainder beyond those exact consequences is established; this is not a judgment against sketch-error bounds in general.
